title: Shortest Distances Between Every Pair
real_world_story: A navigation system serves drivers across a road network and frequently needs the shortest travel distance between many different pairs of locations. To answer these quickly, the system precomputes the shortest distance between every pair of nodes so any future query can be answered instantly.

real_world_connection.input_represents: A weighted graph of locations with roads and travel distances
real_world_connection.query_represents: A frequent request about the shortest distance between two locations
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Precomputing all-pairs shortest distances in advance

problem_statement: Given a weighted, undirected graph with N nodes, an adjacency matrix where a positive value represents the travel distance between two directly connected nodes and 0 represents no direct road, compute the shortest distance between every pair of nodes. Then answer Q queries, each asking for the shortest distance between two nodes.
task: Precompute all-pairs shortest distances and answer each query with the minimum travel distance.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The next N lines each contain N integers forming the adjacency matrix (0 on the diagonal, positive integer travel distance between directly connected nodes, 0 for no direct road). The next line contains an integer Q. The next Q lines each contain two integers U and V indicating a query.
output_format: For each query, print the minimum travel distance between node U and node V. If they are not connected, print -1.

examples.explanation: The shortest distance from node 1 to node 4 is via node 2: 1 + 2 = 3. From node 2 to node 3 it is 1 + 2 + 1 = 3 via node 4, and the shortest distance from a node to itself is 0.

expected_algorithm.name: Floyd-Warshall
expected_algorithm.reason: Floyd-Warshall computes the shortest distance between every pair of nodes in O(N^3), allowing many queries to be answered in constant time afterward.

hint: Start with a distance matrix initialized to the direct edge weights.
For each intermediate node K, check whether traveling through K shortens any pair distance.
Update the matrix until every pair holds its shortest distance.
real_world_takeaway: Precomputing all-pairs distances lets a navigation system answer large numbers of distance queries instantly instead of recomputing each one separately.
